title: BEN Engine — Investor briefing
subtitle: Schreiber AI · BEN Engine Rev 2 · modular data centers from mini racks to 1 MW, asset-light · 2026-11

slides.title: BEN Engine: AI infrastructure that arrives finished
slides.message: Schreiber AI turns a mission profile into an all-in-one data center, power, cooling, compute and controls in one sealed box, built, tested and documented, and keeps watching it. The same system scales to a 2 MW center.
bullets: Rev 2 lineup: BEN 1 mini racks (0.6–1.5 kW, indoors) through BEN 1000 (liquid-first 40 ft, up to 1 MW); BEN 2000 (2 MW hall) is the capability example
Element-proof NEMA 4X / IP66 by default; hardened (H2 severe environment, H3 government) on request
Buy the box, one module, white-label it, or have it managed
Everything in this deck is generated from working software in the repository
slides.notes: Open with the outcome, not the technology. The claim to make: a customer picks a mission profile and gets a finished, commissioned unit with a risk list they saw before the price. The claim to avoid: anything about hardware we have not built yet. Transition: why does this not exist already for small and mid-size businesses?

slides.title: The problem: AI wants to live where the data is, and nobody builds small
slides.message: SMBs face a cloud bill that grows with success, colocation priced for hyperscalers, or a server closet nobody commissioned.
bullets: Wholesale colocation about $196 per kW-month in US primary markets (CBRE, H2 2025)
Traditional builds $10–13 M per MW and 18–30 months (Cushman & Wakefield 2025)
Modular vendors optimise for telcos and hyperscalers, not a 40-person manufacturer or a clinic
Later: the 2 MW regional center for enterprises, hospitals, universities, municipalities and edge colocation, which the same system already sizes and prices (BEN 2000)
BEN 2000 infrastructure-only about $10,200 per kW vs $10,000–13,000 per kW traditional (BOM-based)
slides.notes: All three numbers are cited in docs/investors/MARKET_SOURCES.md with ranges. Say the ranges out loud; investors respect ranges more than point estimates. Transition: the product family. The BEN 2000 figure comes from docs/BOM-ben2000.md and scripts/unit_economics.py (infrastructure-only sell price $16.4 M for 1,600 kW IT); say 'about $10,200 per kW infrastructure-only vs $10,000–13,000 per kW traditional' and that most of that BOM is quote-only estimates.

slides.title: The Rev 2 lineup: BEN 1 to BEN 1000
slides.message: One engineering model from a 0.6 kW mini rack on a shelf to a 1 MW liquid-first 40 ft module. BEN 2000 shows the same system at 2 MW.
bullets: BEN 1 (new): indoor mini rack, 10-inch 8U up to 0.6 kW or 19-inch 12U sound-damped up to 1.5 kW, 120 V plug-in, built in-house
BEN 5, BEN 30, BEN 150 (carried): outdoor cabinet, 10 ft and 20 ft modules, 2–150 kW, cabinet DX, in-row DX or rear-door
BEN 300 (new, dense): 20 ft liquid-first, 150–300 kW, W45 direct liquid, row CDUs N+1, for one or two GB300-class racks
BEN 1000 (new, flagship dense): 40 ft liquid-first all-in-one, 500–1,000 kW, heat-reuse port; BEN 500 carried for existing quotes
Capability example: BEN 2000 prefabricated 2 MW hall. Names are nominal max IT kW; a tier is renamed if its density does not fit
slides.notes: Lead with the two ends the operator asked for: the very low side for tiny businesses (BEN 1) and the dense end (BEN 300, BEN 1000). Everything in the middle is Rev 1 carried unchanged, and Rev 1 quotes reproduce exactly. If the lineup work renamed a dense tier because its target did not fit the interference checks, use the new name here (docs/DENSITY.md). Transition: how dense is dense.

slides.title: Density
slides.message: As dense as a sealed, relocatable box allows, with every figure generated from the configuration and checked against real footprints, not taken from a brochure.
bullets: BEN 300: {{BEN300_KW_PER_RACK}} kW per rack, {{BEN300_KW_PER_M2}} kW per m² of module footprint, {{BEN300_RACKS}} racks in one 20 ft frame
BEN 1000: {{BEN1000_KW_PER_RACK}} kW per rack, {{BEN1000_KW_PER_M2}} kW per m²; power, UPS, CDUs and controls in one 40 ft box
Sourced peers: Delta 20 ft AI container up to 60 kW per rack (AC), ZTE prefab 40 kW per rack, HPE AI Mod POD up to 1.5 MW (AC)

Design values until the BEN 300 lighthouse measures them; 800 VDC stays a gated study, not a claim
slides.notes: Fill the placeholders from docs/DENSITY.md before presenting; never present a slide with braces on it. Peer figures come from docs/research/STATE_OF_THE_ART_2026.md section 3 and are vendor statements, so say 'as published'. The honest positioning: every DC-ready offer is MW-class and every sub-MW container is AC; none publishes leak-to-isolation or redundancy-proof numbers. Our density is a design value until the lighthouse.

slides.title: Mini racks: AI for tiny businesses
slides.message: A tiny business can run private AI on a shelf: one or two AI boxes, a NAS and a firewall, plugged into the wall, set up and watched by Schreiber AI.
bullets: rack10: 10-inch 8U desk or shelf rack up to 0.6 kW; cab12: 19-inch 12U sound-damped office cabinet up to 1.5 kW
120 V plug-in on a dedicated 15 A or 20 A circuit; no pad, no permit, no crane; about 2–3 weeks from order to handover
Built and burned in by Schreiber AI, the one in-house build; noise, heat to room and UPS runtime measured before it ships
Risks in plain words before the price: heat in the closet, circuit overload, noise, theft, untested backups, UPS battery age
Market size: our sources hold no statistic for on-premises tiny-business AI; the 10-unit lighthouse is the first evidence
slides.notes: The buyer is the owner of a studio, a trades business or a small office who wants AI on their own data without hiring IT. What they get is the same discipline as the big units: a site check, a burn-in, measured noise and heat, a handover, BEN Care watching it and a four-line owner maintenance list. Do not quote a market number for this segment; MARKET_SOURCES.md says none was found. Prices come from docs/rev2/UNIT_ECONOMICS.md.

slides.title: Element-proof and hardened
slides.message: Every unit is NEMA 4X / IP66 and hose-tested; H2 and H3 are priced packages that turn a bespoke engineering project into a catalog option.
bullets: H1 Standard (included): IP66 envelope, hose test per UL 50E written into the warranty, C3 coating
H2 Severe environment: flood plinth, marine C5-M coating, dust filtration, hurricane hardware, 67 m/s wind; auto-recommended for coastal, desert, arctic, high-altitude sites
H3 Hardened / government: UL 752 ballistic panels, ASTM F3038 forced-entry doors, mantrap, tamper detection, optional HEMP shield (MIL-STD-188-125-1), CMMC controls pack
Margin lever: hardening lines carry hardware margin above the 28 % base because the buyer pays for a certified, tested envelope and a compliance pack, not steel
slides.notes: Hardening is a margin lever and a market opener (public sector, defence, utilities, coasts). Never say bulletproof, EMP-proof or TEMPEST certified: say UL 752 level, MIL-STD-188-125-1 option, TEMPEST-ready. Vendor certificates are required with every shipment (SUPPLIER_TERMS.md).

slides.title: Why we win: the configuration-driven engineering system
slides.message: Drawings, bill of materials, compliance pack, assembly instructions, digital twin and commissioning report all come from the same configuration.
bullets: config.py sizes power, cooling, structure, mass, PUE; validate() rejects layouts that do not fit
42 issue-for-construction sheets across five tiers (7 per tier, 14 for the BEN 2000 hall) with CTQ/CTP tables, regenerated from the configuration
Assembly instructions in ASD-STE100 for workers with minimal experience
Commissioning script: 12 steps (two forward-architecture steps skipped with the reason on AC units), signed report, SHA-256 of the data
slides.notes: This is the moat. A competitor can buy the same container and UPS. They cannot buy the system that makes every unit identical and testable with few engineers. Demo backup: docs/proposals/ shows a full customer proposal generated by one command. Transition: show the twin.

slides.title: You can run the box before it exists
slides.message: The dashboard that ships in every unit runs in simulation mode: 3-D twin, walkthrough, automated sweeps, fault injection, calibration, CFD, CSV export.
bullets: Six automated sweeps pass on the BEN 150 preset in under a second of compute
Ride-through sweep shows thermal, not battery, is the binding limit (about 2 minutes to ASHRAE A2 max with cooling off) — this drove the mechanical ride-through option
Calibration tools produce GUM uncertainty budgets per sensor
slides.notes: Live demo plan: bash scripts/run_dashboard.sh, open localhost:8080, change tier to BEN 500, inject a cooling failure, watch the standby unit start, run the failover sweep, download the CSV. Recovery plan if the demo fails: the screenshots in docs/media/screens and the sample commissioning report. Caveat to say out loud: the twin's thermal time constants are design values, so the two-minute number is a lower bound until measured on hardware.

slides.title: Compliance is the product
slides.message: The compliance pack is generated per mission profile; it already changed the design three times.
bullets: A2L refrigerants are unusable inside a container at these charges: in-row DX specified with R-513A/R-515B (A1, GWP < 700) ahead of the AIM Act 2027 rule
NFPA 855 / UL 9540 triggers at 20 kWh lithium: BEN 5/30/150 stay under it by default; BEN 500 carries the full package
NEC 110.26 at 480 V drives an electrical vestibule on BEN 150/500
IEC 62443 zones; life safety hardwired and never on the controls network
BEN 2000 is a building: IBC permit, MV service, NFPA 855 battery rooms, NFPA 110 Level 1, SPCC; hardening adds UL 50E / UL 752 / ASTM F3038 / MIL-STD-188-125-1 rows
slides.notes: Investors in this space have been burned by permitting. Lead with the three findings that changed the design; they prove the matrix is not decoration. Edition years are listed in docs/COMPLIANCE.md with what could not be verified.

slides.title: Business model and unit economics
slides.message: Prices are built up from a real bill of materials with a confidence split, not top-down.
bullets: BEN 150 preset (96 kW): infrastructure-only sell price about $0.64 M; all modules including reference GPU compute about $2.6 M at 28 % gross margin
Underlying BOM cost is 79 % vendor-confirmed listings, 21 % engineering estimate (BEN 150); every line carries its status
Recurring: BEN Controls licence per unit per year and managed service at $45 per kW-month (below retail colocation because the customer owns the asset)
Rev 2 tiers from docs/rev2/UNIT_ECONOMICS.md: BEN 1 cab12 {{BEN1_CAB12_SELL_USD}}; infrastructure-only BEN 300 {{BEN300_INFRA_SELL_USD}}, BEN 1000 {{BEN1000_INFRA_SELL_USD}}
slides.notes: The exact table is regenerated by scripts/unit_economics.py into VC_PROPOSITION.md. Be explicit that 'confirmed' in this session means a distributor listing seen in search results on 2026-11-07, not a quote; the 21 RFQ emails queued to Ben@SchreiberAI.com convert those into quotes. Compute dominates the all-modules price; most SMB customers will start infrastructure-only.

slides.title: Asset-light manufacturing: third parties first
slides.message: Contract manufacturers build to our drawings and instructions; integrators sell and install; Schreiber AI owns design, controls, commissioning and operations.
bullets: Leverages the CM's UL 508A listing, certified welders and licensed trades
Hold points and witness points in the process flow; FAT with our commissioning script at their shop
Supplier and CM delay liquidated damages flow back-to-back with customer commitments
Greenfield factory is a later phase with explicit transition criteria
slides.notes: This is where the money does not go: no building. See docs/MANUFACTURING_STRATEGY.md for the CM selection scoring and the transition thresholds. Caveat: no CM has been qualified yet; the RFI is queued.

slides.title: Go-to-market
slides.message: Lighthouse units first, then integrators as the channel, with profile-led marketing that discloses risks before price.
bullets: Lighthouse: ten BEN 1 mini racks with pilot customers and one BEN 300 at a contract manufacturer, producing the data that proves the twin
Integrators and MEP firms bring sites and licensed trades; we bring the system and the white-label controls
Product page leads with the mission profile picker and the risk register; a configured proposal is one click
slides.notes: The product page is in web/ and renders without a backend; the proposal generator is the back end behind the slider. Transition: what the money is for.

slides.title: Rev 2 revamp: what USD 5 M buys
slides.message: The engineering, brand application and documentation revision is done in the repository now. The USD 5 M buys what a repository cannot: hardware, measurements, listings and the people to run them.
bullets: Done now, at no cost to the budget: Rev 2 lineup in the configuration model, brand v2 applied, versioned drawings, BOMs and documents
Hardware: ten BEN 1 units built in-house for pilots; one BEN 300 at a contract manufacturer with FAT, SAT and a 30-day burn-in
Liquid W45 test cell first, 800 VDC cell only as a gated option; BEN Pod v1 production and FCC; UL 508A BEN Controller panels
Brand production (data plates, livery, print, the eight touchpoints), a six-person team, listings and 8 % contingency
Six quarterly gates over 18 months; money is released by measured evidence, not by date
slides.notes: Quote the operator: the base is good, we just need a once-over, and the budget for the once-over is a 5 million revamp. The plan is docs/programs/REV2_REVAMP_PROGRAM.md; it supersedes the 2027–2028 R&D program for budgeting (kept for history). Say plainly that no 800 VDC distribution is listed in November 2026, which is why the DC cell is gated and may return its money to contingency.

bullets: BEN 300 lighthouse $1.45 M · team, 6 FTE for 18 months $1.35 M · liquid W45 test cell $0.40 M · 800 VDC cell, gated option $0.35 M
BEN 1 lighthouse, 10 units built in-house $0.30 M · BEN Pod v1 production and FCC $0.25 M · other listings and compliance $0.23 M

slides.title: What is verified, what is not
slides.message: We tell investors the same thing we tell customers.
bullets: Verified here: configuration model, twin, CFD, calibration, sweeps, commissioning (simulation), BOM generator, drawings, firmware unit tests on host, product page render
Implemented, unverified: EFR32 Pod cross-build (toolchain blocked), edge computer image and PLC project, Pod attestation, all hardware behaviour
Least accurate: thermal ride-through minutes, envelope UA, CFD absolute temperatures, estimate-status prices
Rev 2 tiers (BEN 1, BEN 300, BEN 1000) are design values from the configuration; no Rev 2 hardware exists until the lighthouse units
slides.notes: This slide is the credibility slide. Read docs/VALIDATION.md before presenting and update the bullets to match the latest run. Never soften 'unverified'.
